questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code varies sampling, transport and simulator behavior between environments? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Staging samples 10 percent of devices using zlib.crc32 of the device id instead of random.random() per reading. What is the main effect of that choice?
choices: It makes sampling faster, because crc32 is cheaper than a random number generator
It guarantees exactly 10 percent of devices are selected
A given device is always in or always out of the sample, so selected devices have complete series and the same set is chosen across restarts and instances
It makes the sample cryptographically unpredictable to devices

questions.prompt: The process starts with TELEMETRY_ENV=production, a valid mqtts:// BROKER_URL, and ENABLE_SIMULATOR=1. What happens?
choices: load_profile raises ConfigError, and main prints a message and exits with status 78
The simulator is ignored and ingestion starts normally
Ingestion starts and simulated readings are dropped by the sampling step
The profile falls back to staging, which permits the simulator

questions.prompt: TELEMETRY_ENV=local and BROKER_URL is not set. A normal reading (not an alarm) arrives. What happens?
choices: ConfigError at startup, because every profile requires a broker
The reading is sampled out because local uses a reduced rate
The reading is buffered and sent to the broker on the next two-second flush
The reading is passed to the print-based sink immediately, as a batch of one
